H1-06x.canh: the royal barge on the Thames, afternoon of 2 September 1666
H1-06x.cong_trinh_moc: Old London Bridge with houses on it (if visible); Old St Paul's Gothic tower without dome (if visible); must NOT show any dome
H1-06x.loi: That afternoon, the King and his brother James, Duke of York, take to the river in the royal barge, ordering houses pulled down "apace".

H1-15x.canh: the King and the Duke of York at the fire-lines, Fleet Street, 4 September 1666
H1-15x.cong_trinh_moc: Old St Paul's Gothic tower without dome (if visible); must NOT show any dome
H1-15x.loi: In the last days of the fire, the King and the Duke work the fire-lines themselves — "even laboring in person," Evelyn writes.

H2-02b.canh: a new City plan laid out on a table by a window overlooking the burnt City, September 1666
H2-02b.cong_trinh_moc: Old St Paul's ruined Gothic tower without dome (through the window, if visible); must NOT show any dome
H2-02b.loi: Within days, Christopher Wren hands the King a new City on paper — straight avenues, open squares, a grid. John Evelyn draws another. Robert Hooke, a third. None of them is built.

H2-06b.canh: the Monument column under construction near Pudding Lane, 1675
H2-06b.cong_trinh_moc: the unfinished Monument column (fluted, inside timber scaffolding); must NOT show any dome
H2-06b.loi: Portland stone is so hard to come by that the column takes six years.

H2-09x.canh: the site of the new cathedral on Ludgate Hill, 1675
H2-09x.cong_trinh_moc: must NOT show any dome (the new cathedral is not built yet)
H2-09x.loi: And on Ludgate Hill, where Old St Paul's stood, work starts in 1675 on a new cathedral.

H2-10b.canh: the top of the lantern of St Paul's Cathedral, October 1708
H2-10b.cong_trinh_moc: only old London Bridge (with houses) across the Thames; no other dome; St Paul's lantern in the foreground
H2-10b.loi: The last stone of the lantern is set in 1708 — by Wren's son, Christopher.

H5-02b.canh: the Barbican towers under construction beside London Wall, 1968
H5-02b.cong_trinh_moc: St Paul's Cathedral dome (only if visible); Barbican towers unfinished
H5-02b.loi: and on the ruins of Cripplegate, from the mid-1960s, the towers of the Barbican.

H5-02s.cong_trinh_moc: St Paul's Cathedral dome (only if visible); Barbican towers (completed)
H5-02s.loi: Where the bombs hit hardest, it is bold: a new road, London Wall, built in the 1950s; and on the ruins of Cripplegate, from the mid-1960s, the towers of the Barbican.

H5-04c.canh: the cluster of City towers seen from Leadenhall Street, 2026
H5-04c.cong_trinh_moc: Leadenhall Building (tapering wedge); 30 St Mary Axe; 22 Bishopsgate (only those in the input)
H5-04c.loi: And in this century, a cluster of towers climbs to the east, around Bishopsgate and Leadenhall Street.

H5-05d.canh: a protected view of St Paul's dome across the Thames, 2026
H5-05d.cong_trinh_moc: St Paul's Cathedral dome (with open sky behind it); City towers to the right (only those in the input)
H5-05d.loi: The St Paul's Heights still apply, alongside a set of protected views across London — the farthest from a hill in Richmond Park, ten miles away.

H5-05b.canh: Fleet Street looking east to the dome, 2026
H5-05b.cong_trinh_moc: St Paul's Cathedral dome with open sky behind it; Leadenhall Building must NOT appear behind the dome
H5-05b.loi: The Leadenhall Building tapers as it rises, so that from Fleet Street, the dome still has open sky behind it.
